state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> [WATCHME(the_beater_holds_the_claim):waiting] -> PROVED
intention: The process beating is the process holding the claim, and a mismatch is a permanent loud record rather than something a human happens to notice.
why: On 2026-08-18 two ground loops held the device's address for roughly 80 minutes - pid 4190113 holding the flock on devices/ground_loop/0/run.lock while pid 973171 did the beating - and the only reason anyone knows is that Akien looked. The singleton guard is not what failed: claim_singleton takes fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB) in one syscall, the kernel releases it when the holder dies, and main() claims BEFORE constructing the device, so a loop started through the runner cannot be a second loop. What the guard cannot cover is a beater that never went through the runner - and nothing anywhere compares the two. The invariant was already half-instrumented on both sides for the whole incident: the beat writes its pid into liveness.json every second, and the kernel has named the flock holder in /proc/locks all along. Nothing had to be built to KNOW there were two loops; something had to be built to LOOK.
how: The claim holder is a two-line kernel read: stat the lock for its inode, find that inode in /proc/locks, which names the holding pid directly. MEASURED 2026-08-18: inode 29118926 -> 'FLOCK ADVISORY WRITE 360391', and 360391 is exactly the pid liveness.json carries. The probe asks the kernel who holds the claim, reads the pid the beat itself wrote, and compares - three outcomes, and the third is what this node exists for: they match (green); nobody holds the lock while liveness is fresh (a beater outside the runner, loud); a DIFFERENT pid holds it than the one beating (the 80-minute condition, loud and permanent through the trouble lane). It berths as a ground_loop probe so it rides the beat it is about and needs no clock of its own, and it reports INABILITY rather than green when it cannot read /proc/locks.
traces_to: Law 3 and Law 10 together: the condition WAS measurable the whole time it went unmeasured - two numbers, both already on the machine - so 'nobody noticed' was never a fact about the world, it was an instrument nobody built. And Law 7: an error is loud at diagnostic surfaces and permanent in records of truth; a duplicate loop is currently loud nowhere.
gates: code-seam's invariant pair plus its class gates. PROVE GATE: the tester runs the node's proof, verdict and seal from the same hand. The non-hollow tooth is the INDUCED MISMATCH - the proof manufactures the condition (a claimant that is not the beater, under an isolated instance root) and asserts the record appears naming both pids. A hollow build that always reported 'match' passes a happy-path test and fails this one, which is why the fixture is the tooth rather than a green on a healthy host. Second tooth: with /proc/locks made unreadable, the probe reports inability, not green. DURABILITY GATE: not done until tested AND committed. FEEDS BACK TO ORIGIN ON FAILURE: a red routes to this node; a mismatch found in the WILD routes to the trouble lane, which is the node's own output path.
falsifier: DONE when a deliberately induced mismatch - a second beater started without the runner's claim, under an isolated instance root so the instrument does not seed the tree it reads - produces a permanent record naming BOTH pids, within one beat of the condition existing, with nobody looking. WRONG INTENT if it becomes a KILLER: this node makes the condition loud, it does not arbitrate who dies. Killing the wrong one of two loops is worse than knowing there are two. Also wrong if the check migrates into the guard - the guard's job is the claim, and a claimant cannot audit a beater it never met.
horizon: the same day the probe lands - no clock, no live host, no waiting for a recurrence. The induced mismatch is a fixture, which is what keeps this from being a watch provable only by the incident happening again.
children: none, because the instrument is one comparison of two numbers that already exist - a stat plus a read of /proc/locks against a pid liveness already writes. There is no second mechanism hiding under it, which is exactly what distinguished it from a-beat-costs-what-changed, cast minutes earlier, where two mechanisms did hide under one number.

watchme.trigger: every beat - the probe rides the pulse it is about. Two reads (a stat plus one small file) add nothing measurable to a beat that currently costs seconds, and it needs no clock of its own, which is the point of berthing it here.
watchme.enough: NOT satisfied by a green on a healthy host - that is the state the incident already looked like from outside. Enough when it has seen the induced mismatch go loud AND has survived one real loop restart (the moment the pid legitimately changes, the obvious false-positive shape and the one thing that would teach an operator to ignore it).
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier, carrying BOTH pids, the lock's inode, and which of the three outcomes was seen - so a red arrives already saying which condition it is, rather than needing the host inspected while it is still true.
watchme.nexus: the ground_loop device's own tree - a fact about the heartbeat's identity, the same nexus its liveness and residency watches teach.
watchme.consumer: the trouble lane on a mismatch (the permanence half of Law 7 - the record must outlive the condition, because the condition's evidence is exactly what died last time), and the ground_loop pane for the standing answer.

provenance: Cast 2026-08-18 at Akien's agreement to /sorted the ground-loop defects the post-OOM restart surfaced. Discovered while restarting the loop off the terminal window, which is why it is a sibling of the-heartbeat-outlives-its-caller rather than a child of it.

distinctions_recorded.against_the_proved_singleton_ticket: an-entry-point-starts-the-loop-only-once (PROVED 2026-08-09) names 'two entry points launched simultaneously produce TWO loops' as its expensive falsifier direction, and that is the condition observed. Whys compared: its why is that a user starting a second entry point must not get a second loop, and its proof covers loops started THROUGH the entry points. Today's beater did not come through one. The population differs, so the verdict stands - a proof is not falsified by a case outside its stated population - and this node EXTENDS the ticket's reach rather than reopening it.
distinctions_recorded.against_the_guard: No conflict with guard.py's charter, and the boundary is clean: the guard owns the CLAIM, this node owns the AUDIT. They cannot be one component because the guard runs once at start while the mismatch appears later. And the probe carries no authority (Law 6) - it reads two numbers and writes a record, and gates nothing.

open_at_cast: THREE assumptions, each with a named measurement rather than an argument. (1) That /proc/locks is readable and complete for this user's own flocks - measured at n=1 on this host, unmeasured elsewhere, so the probe must REPORT inability rather than pass; a check that goes green when it cannot read is the coin-toss red. (2) That liveness.json's pid is written by the beating process ITSELF and not by a starter on its behalf - UNVERIFIED, and the FIRST thing the build establishes by reading liveness.py's writer, because getting it wrong yields a check that is green while the condition it names is live. (3) That the lock file is never replaced - guard.py's docstring asserts it in prose ('the winner's claim rides one inode for the process's whole life') and nothing enforces it; if anything ever replaced that file, a second claimant would flock a fresh inode and win, and both loops would believe they hold the claim. Measured true today (run.lock mtime 2026-08-09 11:48). The probe already reads that inode, so witnessing it is one line.
deliberately_unanswered: WHAT SHOULD HAPPEN when two loops are found. This node makes the condition loud and refuses to arbitrate, because killing the wrong one of two loops is worse than knowing there are two. If an arbiter is wanted it is a second node carrying a rule about which claim wins. FOR AKIEN.
destroyed_measurement: The MECHANISM that produced the 2026-08-18 double loop is unmeasured and stays that way - the evidence died with the process killed during the restart. Recorded as a destroyed measurement rather than replaced with a plausible story. Had the loudness this node builds existed, the cause would have been in the record, which is the argument for the node in one sentence.
sibling_note: The two pids in the incident (4190113, 973171) are both larger than any pid alive now, so they come from an earlier boot's numbering. Recorded because a reader matching them against today's process table will find nothing and may conclude it never happened.
